sections.h2: Which county collects property tax on an Amarillo house?
sections.html:
The answer turns on the county line. Amarillo spans Potter County and Randall County, and each county's tax assessor-collector bills and collects for its own part, while a single appraisal district, the Potter-Randall Appraisal District, sets values for both.

The Comptroller's county directories list the offices and the taxing units that appear on an Amarillo bill: the City of Amarillo, Amarillo Independent School District, Amarillo Junior College District, the county itself and, depending on location, units such as Bushland ISD, River Road ISD, Highland Park ISD, Canyon ISD and High Plains Underground Water Conservation District No. 1.

  • Potter County Tax Assessor-Collector: 900 S. Polk St., Suite 106, Amarillo, phone 806-342-2600, mail to P.O. Box 2289, Amarillo 79105-2289.
  • Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector: 501 16th St., Suite 200, Canyon, phone 806-468-5540, mail to P.O. Box 997, Canyon 79015-0997.
  • Potter-Randall Appraisal District: 5701 Hollywood Rd., Amarillo, phone 806-358-1601, for values, exemptions and protests in both counties.

sections.h2: What is the City of Amarillo property tax rate?
sections.html:
The city's total rate is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation, made up of $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for existing debt. Council adopted it with the 2026/2027 budget in a 4-1 vote at a special meeting in late September 2026.

By the city's own count, the budget raises $2,063,963 more in property tax revenue than last year, a 2.58 percent increase, and $1,295,675 of that comes from property added to the roll this year. The city says the rate is effectively up 2.9 percent for maintenance and operations, which it puts at about $9 on a $100,000 home.

The same city page charts what Amarillo returns to businesses through economic development deals: property tax rebates under Chapter 311 and Chapter 380 agreements, and abatements under Chapter 312. For 2024/2025 it lists $1,143,899 abated by the city itself out of $2,959,496 abated by all participating taxing entities.

sections.h2: When are Amarillo property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed around October 1, and most owners have until January 31. An unpaid balance on February 1 is delinquent, and that is when the 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are charged.

From there, the penalty goes up 1 percent a month through June and reaches 12 percent on July 1, with interest continuing at 1 percent a month. A taxing unit under an attorney contract can add up to 20 percent for collection. Owners 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans may split a homestead bill into installments.

A homeowner who falls behind should call the Potter or Randall County office right away. Homestead payment plans of up to 36 months exist at some collectors. To seek a waiver of the penalty and interest, pay promptly and put the request in writing before day 181 after the delinquency date.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to Amarillo homeowners?
sections.html:
Texas lets a homeowner subtract $140,000 from the value used for school taxes, whether the district is Amarillo ISD or another that serves the address. People 65 or older or disabled get an added $60,000 for schools, and the school tax on their home is frozen at the first qualifying level.

Cities, counties and colleges may add local exemptions of up to 20 percent of value, so check which ones Amarillo, the two counties and Amarillo Junior College District have adopted. A disabled veteran's exemption runs from $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating up to $12,000 at 70 percent or more, and a 100 percent rating can exempt the whole residence homestead.

  • Applications go to the Potter-Randall Appraisal District, which handles both counties.
  • The general deadline is before May 1, though some veteran claims can be filed up to five years after the delinquency date.
  • Heirs not named on a recorded deed can claim a homestead with an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: How can an Amarillo owner protest the appraised value?
sections.html:
A written protest goes to the Potter-Randall Appraisal District. The cutoff is May 15, or 30 days after you receive the value notice when that falls later, and homestead notices start arriving about April 1.

The appraisal review board starts hearing cases about mid-May. Only the market value is open to challenge, since the appraisal district does not set rates. A homestead's assessed value can climb only 10 percent a year after the first qualifying year, even when market value jumps faster. A loss at the board leaves three paths: district court, binding arbitration, or, for values over $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

Because the appraisal district is one office for two counties, you do not file separately by county. Pay at least the undisputed amount to the Potter or Randall collector before the delinquency date while the protest is pending.

sections.h2: What should an Amarillo seller know about the local market?
sections.html:
Amarillo's July 2025 estimate from the Census Bureau is 205,130 people, compared with 200,393 in the 2020 count and 190,695 in 2010. The city covers 102.30 land square miles, about 1,958.8 people to each.

About 59.7 percent of homes are owner occupied, with a 2020 to 2024 median value of $196,900. Renters pay a median $1,092, owners with a mortgage $1,654 a month, and the median household earns $65,912. A bachelor's degree is held by 26.6 percent of adults, and the city has 10,973 veterans and 79,741 households averaging 2.50 people. Retail sales reached $5,722,271 thousand in 2022 and health care and social assistance receipts $2,777,390 thousand, while the average commute is 19.6 minutes. About 18.0 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance.

Census figures also show 89.2 percent of households with broadband and 11.0 percent of residents born outside the United States.

A Texas tax lien attaches on January 1 and follows the property, and the person who owned it that day stays liable even after a sale. Title cannot clear until back taxes are settled. If you owe both Potter and Randall accounts, for example on adjoining parcels, ask each tax office for a separate payoff letter before closing.

sections.h2: What happens if an Amarillo house is sold at a tax sale?
sections.html:
Texas lets the taxing units foreclose on the lien and auction the property, usually through the constable or an agent the unit hires. There is no statewide list of sales, so watch the Potter and Randall county sites and clerk postings.

A former owner may still get the house back for a limited time. For a homestead, farm or mineral interest, the redemption period is two years from the date the purchaser's deed is filed, and the redeeming owner pays the purchase price plus a 25 percent premium in the first year or 50 percent in the second, along with the recording fee, taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Other property has a 180-day window and a premium of no more than 25 percent. Money left after the sale belongs to the former owner for two years.

  • Ask the purchaser for an itemized list of costs; it is due within 10 days of a written request.
  • Keep every payoff letter, since taxes owed for different years are billed separately.
  • Call before January 31 if you can, because the penalty starts the next day.

faqs.q: Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?
faqs.a: Both. The city lies across the two counties, so your bill comes from the county where the parcel sits. Potter-Randall Appraisal District values property in both.

faqs.q: What is the Amarillo city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The adopted total is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation: $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for debt. The budget raises $2,063,963 more in property tax revenue than last year's.

faqs.q: When do Amarillo property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: They go delinquent on February 1 after a January 31 due date. A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added at once, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call to pay Amarillo property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the county tax office for your parcel: Potter County at 806-342-2600 or Randall County at 806-468-5540. Use the Potter-Randall Appraisal District at 806-358-1601 for value and exemption questions.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Amarillo?
faqs.a: The school district share drops by $140,000 of homestead value, and by $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Cities and counties may layer on their own exemptions of up to 20 percent.
